entries.summary: Executed the feasible RR-002 slice in the macOS workspace by hardening Windows CI and scripted validation instead of claiming real hardware validation that was not run.
Added a headless Windows smoke mode plus package-script validation so CI can exercise the packaged executable itself without pretending tray or capture UX was validated.
Treated the Windows-targeted compile failure as a real RR-002 defect and fixed it in scope instead of deferring it behind the broader runtime-validation risk.
Kept RR-002 on phase/RR-002-windows-runtime-hardening and cherry-picked only the targeted validation-fix commit so the phase record stays isolated from unrelated feature-branch work.

Treated the inherited diagnostics-redaction failure and packaged-smoke exit-code bug as RR-002 work because they blocked the package/runtime signal, then reran DiagnosticsLoggerTests and release_smoke_test.sh on the phase branch before updating state.
Extended RR-002 package validation by checking packaged-file hashes against the publish outputs and by uploading a machine-readable Windows validation manifest plus smoke report from the CI run.

Captured the Windows takeover path in-repo with a dedicated handoff doc, a handoff script, and a CI-produced handoff artifact so Codex on Windows can continue RR-002 from repo state instead of chat-only context.

Adjusted the RR-002 Windows handoff, package, and validation scripts for Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility and self-contained publish output because the real-machine baseline could not be executed honestly until the scripts stopped relying on PowerShell 7-only features and a preinstalled desktop runtime.

Closed RISK-WIN-001 using real Windows evidence instead of CI-only inference: the tray icon appeared in the system-tray overflow, duplicate launches focused the primary instance, recording ran against a Ready microphone, screenshot overlay region capture wrote deterministic artifacts, and hotkeys worked from another focused desktop app.

Kept alternate keyboard layout coverage and signed public-release proof explicitly unresolved after the April 4, 2026 Windows pass because this machine exposed only one installed input layout and the RR-002 runtime work did not exercise signed installer or release automation.
Captured the GitHub Actions Node 20 deprecation warnings from the successful phase-branch run as a separate follow-up risk instead of expanding RR-002 into workflow-runtime maintenance.

Implemented retry-needed preserved-session recovery and generated review summary support on the RR-002 branch immediately because both features were already local, testable, and blocking obvious macOS parity inside the review loop.

Used a lightweight Help And Support window plus native shell-launch actions for docs, changelog, releases, issues, repository, support, and debug bundles instead of turning the Windows tray app into a larger always-open shell.

Kept the Windows accessibility and permission-guidance work incremental and evidence-backed by adding labels, live status announcements, default or cancel behavior, and Windows settings links, while leaving assistive-technology runtime proof for later validation instead of overclaiming it.

Stopped runtime and provider parity at the honest machine boundary: this Windows host could prove the no-key recovery and debug-bundle paths, but it had no provider credentials, only one installed keyboard layout, and only one detected display adapter.

Chose Inno Setup for the Windows public-release scaffold and made the Phase B script emit a blocked status artifact whenever installer or signing prerequisites are missing, rather than pretending the app has public release parity.

Validated the Windows GitHub export path against a disposable private GitHub repository created under the maintainer account, then closed the created issue after proof so the validation did not touch the main product repo.

Used a small Windows-only validation harness against the production storage and export services to prove session deletion and corrupted-local-state bundle safety on this machine without adding more permanent repo surface area.

Reran the Phase B public-release script after the WIN-010 follow-up validation and confirmed the public path is still honestly blocked only on installer and signing prerequisites, not on build or test failures.
